title: Transformations: Translations, Reflections, Rotations and Dilations
standard_text: G.3A describe and perform transformations of figures in a plane using coordinate notation; G.3B determine the image or pre-image of a given two-dimensional figure under a composition of rigid transformations, a composition of non-rigid transformations, and a composition of both, including dilations where the center can be any point in the plane; G.3C identify the sequence of transformations that will carry a given pre-image onto an image on and off the coordinate plane
meta_desc: Free Geometry transformation worksheets for Texas TEKS G.3A–G.3C: translations, reflections, rotations, compositions and dilations with any center. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Rigid transformations keep size and shape.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Translation (x, y) → (x + a, y + b).
  • Reflection over the x-axis: (x, −y); over the y-axis: (−x, y); over y = x: (y, x).
  • Rotation 90° counterclockwise: (−y, x); 180°: (−x, −y).
  • Dilation by k from center (a, b): move the center to the origin, multiply by k, move back.
  • Rigid transformations keep size and shape; dilations keep shape only.

Examples

Example

Rotate (3, −2) 90° counterclockwise

(x, y) → (−y, x)

Answer: (2, 3)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Changing the wrong coordinateReflect over the x-axis: change y.
Rotating the wrong wayCounterclockwise is the positive direction.
Dilating from the originUse the given center.

faq.a: Describe and perform transformations of figures in a plane using coordinate notation.

Determine the image or pre-image of a given two-dimensional figure under a composition of rigid transformations, a composition of non-rigid transformations, and a composition of both, including dilations where the center can be any point in the plane.
Identify the sequence of transformations that will carry a given pre-image onto an image on and off the coordinate plane.

items.q: A translation maps A(7, −1) to A′(10, 3). Which rule describes it?
A translation maps A(5, 2) to A′(3, 5). Which rule describes it?
A translation maps A(2, 7) to A′(−2, 13). Which rule describes it?
A translation by the rule (x, y) → (x − 3, y + 6) maps point A to A′(−2, 0). What are the coordinates of A?
items.e: Undo the translation: subtract −3 from x and 6 from y. A = (1, −6).

items.q: A translation maps A(−3, −4) to A′(−4, −6). Which rule describes it?
Point A(4, 8) is translated by the rule (x, y) → (x + 3, y + 6). What are the coordinates of A′?
A translation by the rule (x, y) → (x − 6, y + 2) maps point A to A′(−2, −1). What are the coordinates of A?
items.e: Undo the translation: subtract −6 from x and 2 from y. A = (4, −3).

items.q: Point A(−2, 4) is translated by the rule (x, y) → (x − 2, y + 3). What are the coordinates of A′?
Point A(−7, 8) is translated by the rule (x, y) → (x − 2, y + 7). What are the coordinates of A′?
Point A(−6, 4) is translated by the rule (x, y) → (x − 4, y − 5). What are the coordinates of A′?
A translation maps A(2, 5) to A′(−2, 12). Which rule describes it?
A translation by the rule (x, y) → (x − 3, y + 1) maps point A to A′(1, 7). What are the coordinates of A?
items.e: Undo the translation: subtract −3 from x and 1 from y. A = (4, 6).

items.q: A translation maps A(5, −1) to A′(−1, 6). Which rule describes it?
Point A(8, 6) is translated by the rule (x, y) → (x − 1, y − 5). What are the coordinates of A′?
A translation maps A(2, −1) to A′(−4, −4). Which rule describes it?
Point A(−2, −1) is translated by the rule (x, y) → (x + 6, y + 3). What are the coordinates of A′?
Point A(2, 1) is translated by the rule (x, y) → (x + 4, y + 2). What are the coordinates of A′?
A translation by the rule (x, y) → (x + 1, y − 6) maps point A to A′(4, −1). What are the coordinates of A?
items.e: Undo the translation: subtract 1 from x and −6 from y. A = (3, 5).

items.q: Point A(−1, −8) is translated by the rule (x, y) → (x − 5, y + 1). What are the coordinates of A′?
A translation maps A(1, −7) to A′(2, −11). Which rule describes it?
Reflect A(8, −5) over the line y = −3. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: A is 2 units below y = −3. Go the same distance to the other side: y = −1. The x-coordinate stays. (8, −1).

items.q: Reflect A(8, −4) over the line y = −1. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: A is 3 units below y = −1. Go the same distance to the other side: y = 2. The x-coordinate stays. (8, 2).

items.q: Reflect A(6, 7) over the line x = 3. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: A is 3 units right of x = 3. Go the same distance to the other side: x = 0. The y-coordinate stays. (0, 7).

items.q: Reflect A(2, −8) over the y-axis. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Reflection over the y-axis: (x, y) → (−x, y). A′ = (−2, −8).

items.q: Reflect A(2, 6) over the y-axis. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Reflection over the y-axis: (x, y) → (−x, y). A′ = (−2, 6).

items.q: Reflect A(−2, −8) over the x-axis. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Reflection over the x-axis: (x, y) → (x, −y). A′ = (−2, 8).

items.q: Reflect A(7, −6) over the line y = 4. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: A is 10 units below y = 4. Go the same distance to the other side: y = 14. The x-coordinate stays. (7, 14).

items.q: Reflect A(−1, 8) over the line y = x. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Reflection over the line y = x: (x, y) → (y, x). A′ = (8, −1).

items.q: Reflect A(−6, −1) over the line y = −2. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: A is 1 unit above y = −2. Go the same distance to the other side: y = −3. The x-coordinate stays. (−6, −3).

items.q: Reflect A(−4, −2) over the line x = 1. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: A is 5 units left of x = 1. Go the same distance to the other side: x = 6. The y-coordinate stays. (6, −2).

items.q: Reflect A(−1, 4) over the line y = x. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Reflection over the line y = x: (x, y) → (y, x). A′ = (4, −1).

items.q: Reflect A(−6, 7) over the line y = 2. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: A is 5 units above y = 2. Go the same distance to the other side: y = −3. The x-coordinate stays. (−6, −3).

items.q: Reflect A(−3, 6) over the line y = 2. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: A is 4 units above y = 2. Go the same distance to the other side: y = −2. The x-coordinate stays. (−3, −2).

items.q: Reflect A(7, −6) over the x-axis. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Reflection over the x-axis: (x, y) → (x, −y). A′ = (7, 6).

items.q: Reflect A(−4, −2) over the line y = x. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Reflection over the line y = x: (x, y) → (y, x). A′ = (−2, −4).

items.q: Reflect A(3, −5) over the x-axis. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Reflection over the x-axis: (x, y) → (x, −y). A′ = (3, 5).

items.q: Reflect A(−3, −2) over the line y = x. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Reflection over the line y = x: (x, y) → (y, x). A′ = (−2, −3).

items.q: Reflect A(−2, −1) over the line y = 3. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: A is 4 units below y = 3. Go the same distance to the other side: y = 7. The x-coordinate stays. (−2, 7).

items.q: Reflect A(4, −7) over the line y = x. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Reflection over the line y = x: (x, y) → (y, x). A′ = (−7, 4).

items.q: Reflect A(6, −2) over the x-axis. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Reflection over the x-axis: (x, y) → (x, −y). A′ = (6, 2).

items.q: Rotate A(−8, −1) 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Rotation 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). A′ = (−1, 8). (90° clockwise is the same as 270° counterclockwise.)

items.q: Rotate A(4, 2) 180° about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
Rotate A(8, −7) 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Rotation 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). A′ = (−7, −8). (90° clockwise is the same as 270° counterclockwise.)

items.q: Rotate A(−8, −5) 90° counterclockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Rotation 90° counterclockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). A′ = (5, −8).

items.q: Rotate A(3, −6) 90° counterclockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Rotation 90° counterclockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). A′ = (6, 3).

items.q: Rotate A(−2, 3) 90° counterclockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Rotation 90° counterclockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). A′ = (−3, −2).

items.q: Rotate A(−6, 2) 180° about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
Rotate A(7, 1) 180° about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
A rotation about the origin maps A(5, −6) to A′(−6, −5). Which rotation is it?
items.e: Test the rules: (x, y) → (y, −x) gives (−6, −5). 90° clockwise.

items.q: Rotate A(2, 7) 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Rotation 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). A′ = (7, −2). (90° clockwise is the same as 270° counterclockwise.)

items.q: A rotation about the origin maps A(5, 8) to A′(8, −5). Which rotation is it?
items.e: Test the rules: (x, y) → (y, −x) gives (8, −5). 90° clockwise.

items.q: Rotate A(−1, 4) 90° counterclockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Rotation 90° counterclockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). A′ = (−4, −1).

items.q: Rotate A(1, −7) 180° about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
A rotation about the origin maps A(1, −4) to A′(4, 1). Which rotation is it?
items.e: Test the rules: (x, y) → (−y, x) gives (4, 1). 90° counterclockwise.

items.q: Rotate A(−4, −3) 90° clockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Rotation 90° clockwise: (x, y) → (y, −x). A′ = (−3, 4). (90° clockwise is the same as 270° counterclockwise.)

items.q: Rotate A(8, −5) 90° counterclockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Rotation 90° counterclockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). A′ = (5, 8).

items.q: A rotation about the origin maps A(6, −7) to A′(−7, −6). Which rotation is it?
items.e: Test the rules: (x, y) → (y, −x) gives (−7, −6). 90° clockwise.

items.q: A rotation about the origin maps A(1, −3) to A′(3, 1). Which rotation is it?
items.e: Test the rules: (x, y) → (−y, x) gives (3, 1). 90° counterclockwise.

items.q: Rotate A(−6, −3) 90° counterclockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Rotation 90° counterclockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x). A′ = (3, −6).

items.q: A rotation about the origin maps A(−5, −8) to A′(−8, 5). Which rotation is it?
items.e: Test the rules: (x, y) → (y, −x) gives (−8, 5). 90° clockwise.

items.q: Which transformation maps triangle ABC to triangle A′B′C′?
c: A rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin
A rotation of 90° counterclockwise about the origin
items.e: Compare a vertex: A(2, 1) goes to A′(−2, 1). y stays and x changes sign. A reflection over the y-axis.

items.q: Start with A(5, −3): translate it by (x, y) → (x + 4, y − 4), then rotate it 90° counterclockwise about the origin. Where does A end up?
items.e: Do the steps in order. After the first step: (9, −7). After the second step: (7, 9). The order matters: the other order gives (7, 1).

items.q: Start with A(6, −4): reflect it over the x-axis, then translate it by (x, y) → (x + 4, y − 3). Where does A end up?
items.e: Do the steps in order. After the first step: (6, 4). After the second step: (10, 1). The order matters: the other order gives (10, 7).

items.q: Start with A(−6, −2): rotate it 180° about the origin, then translate it by (x, y) → (x − 1, y − 3). Where does A end up?
items.e: Do the steps in order. After the first step: (6, 2). After the second step: (5, −1). The order matters: the other order gives (7, 5).

items.q: Which transformation maps triangle ABC to triangle A′B′C′?
c: A rotation of 90° counterclockwise about the origin
A rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin
items.e: Compare a vertex: A(2, 1) goes to A′(2, −1). x stays and y changes sign. A reflection over the x-axis.

items.q: Which transformation maps triangle ABC to triangle A′B′C′?
c: A rotation of 180° about the origin
A rotation of 90° counterclockwise about the origin
items.e: Compare a vertex: A(1, 2) goes to A′(−1, −2). Both coordinates change sign. A rotation of 180° about the origin.

items.q: Which transformation maps triangle ABC to triangle A′B′C′?
c: A rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin
items.e: Compare a vertex: A(4, 1) goes to A′(1, 4). The coordinates swap. A reflection over the line y = x.

items.q: Start with A(1, −5): reflect it over the x-axis, then translate it by (x, y) → (x + 5, y + 3). Where does A end up?
items.e: Do the steps in order. After the first step: (1, 5). After the second step: (6, 8). The order matters: the other order gives (6, 2).

items.q: Which transformation maps triangle ABC to triangle A′B′C′?
c: A rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin
A rotation of 90° counterclockwise about the origin
items.e: Compare a vertex: A(2, 2) goes to A′(2, −2). x stays and y changes sign. A reflection over the x-axis.

items.q: Start with A(5, 4): rotate it 180° about the origin, then translate it by (x, y) → (x + 1, y + 3). Where does A end up?
items.e: Do the steps in order. After the first step: (−5, −4). After the second step: (−4, −1). The order matters: the other order gives (−6, −7).

items.q: Start with A(6, −2): rotate it 180° about the origin, then translate it by (x, y) → (x − 2, y + 2). Where does A end up?
items.e: Do the steps in order. After the first step: (−6, 2). After the second step: (−8, 4). The order matters: the other order gives (−4, 0).

items.q: Which transformation maps triangle ABC to triangle A′B′C′?
c: A rotation of 90° counterclockwise about the origin
A rotation of 180° about the origin
items.e: Compare a vertex: A(1, 1) goes to A′(−1, 1). y stays and x changes sign. A reflection over the y-axis.

items.q: Which transformation maps triangle ABC to triangle A′B′C′?
c: A rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin
items.e: Compare a vertex: A(1, 1) goes to A′(−5, 2). Every point moves the same way and the triangle keeps its orientation. A translation by (x, y) → (x − 6, y + 1).

items.q: Start with A(−4, −1): rotate it 90° counterclockwise about the origin, then translate it by (x, y) → (x − 2, y − 2). Where does A end up?
items.e: Do the steps in order. After the first step: (1, −4). After the second step: (−1, −6). The order matters: the other order gives (3, −6).

items.q: Start with A(5, 1): rotate it 180° about the origin, then translate it by (x, y) → (x + 4, y + 3). Where does A end up?
items.e: Do the steps in order. After the first step: (−5, −1). After the second step: (−1, 2). The order matters: the other order gives (−9, −4).

items.q: Which transformation maps triangle ABC to triangle A′B′C′?
c: A rotation of 90° counterclockwise about the origin
A rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin
A rotation of 180° about the origin
items.e: Compare a vertex: A(2, 1) goes to A′(−2, −1). Both coordinates change sign. A rotation of 180° about the origin.

items.q: Which transformation maps triangle ABC to triangle A′B′C′?
c: A rotation of 180° about the origin
A rotation of 90° counterclockwise about the origin
items.e: Compare a vertex: A(1, 1) goes to A′(−1, 1). (x, y) → (−y, x). A rotation of 90° counterclockwise about the origin.

items.q: Which transformation maps triangle ABC to triangle A′B′C′?
c: A rotation of 90° counterclockwise about the origin
A rotation of 180° about the origin
items.e: Compare a vertex: A(1, 2) goes to A′(−2, 1). (x, y) → (−y, x). A rotation of 90° counterclockwise about the origin.

items.q: Start with A(3, −1): translate it by (x, y) → (x + 2, y − 5), then rotate it 90° counterclockwise about the origin. Where does A end up?
items.e: Do the steps in order. After the first step: (5, −6). After the second step: (6, 5). The order matters: the other order gives (3, −2).

items.q: Start with A(6, 4): reflect it over the x-axis, then translate it by (x, y) → (x − 4, y + 2). Where does A end up?
items.e: Do the steps in order. After the first step: (6, −4). After the second step: (2, −2). The order matters: the other order gives (2, −6).

items.q: Dilate A(3, −8) by a scale factor of 12 with center C(−3, −4). Where is A′?
items.e: Find the step from C to A: (6, −4). Multiply it by 12: (3, −2). Add it to C: (0, −6).

items.q: Dilate A(−4, −3) by a scale factor of 12 with center C(4, −1). Where is A′?
items.e: Find the step from C to A: (−8, −2). Multiply it by 12: (−4, −1). Add it to C: (0, −2).

items.q: Dilate A(0, −1) by a scale factor of 2 with center C(−4, 1). Where is A′?
items.e: Find the step from C to A: (4, −2). Multiply it by 2: (8, −4). Add it to C: (4, −3).

items.q: Dilate A(12, 9) by a scale factor of 12 with center C(4, 1). Where is A′?
items.e: Find the step from C to A: (8, 8). Multiply it by 12: (4, 4). Add it to C: (8, 5).

items.q: Dilate A(10, −6) by a scale factor of 12 with center C(4, −4). Where is A′?
items.e: Find the step from C to A: (6, −2). Multiply it by 12: (3, −1). Add it to C: (7, −5).

items.q: Dilate A(−9, −6) by a scale factor of 12 with center C(−3, 0). Where is A′?
items.e: Find the step from C to A: (−6, −6). Multiply it by 12: (−3, −3). Add it to C: (−6, −3).

items.q: Dilate A(3, 5) by a scale factor of 12 with center C(1, −1). Where is A′?
items.e: Find the step from C to A: (2, 6). Multiply it by 12: (1, 3). Add it to C: (2, 2).

items.q: Dilate A(−2, −4) by a scale factor of 12 with center C(2, 0). Where is A′?
items.e: Find the step from C to A: (−4, −4). Multiply it by 12: (−2, −2). Add it to C: (0, −2).

items.q: Dilate A(−5, −1) by a scale factor of 2 with center C(−3, 1). Where is A′?
items.e: Find the step from C to A: (−2, −2). Multiply it by 2: (−4, −4). Add it to C: (−7, −3).

items.q: Dilate A(−3, 7) by a scale factor of 2 with center C(1, 3). Where is A′?
items.e: Find the step from C to A: (−4, 4). Multiply it by 2: (−8, 8). Add it to C: (−7, 11).

items.q: Point A(6, 7) is dilated by a scale factor of 4 with center at the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Multiply both coordinates by 4: (4 × 6, 4 × 7) = (24, 28).

items.q: Point A(−5, −8) is dilated by a scale factor of 2 with center at the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Multiply both coordinates by 2: (2 × −5, 2 × −8) = (−10, −16).

items.q: Point A(−1, 8) is dilated by a scale factor of 2 with center at the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Multiply both coordinates by 2: (2 × −1, 2 × 8) = (−2, 16).

items.q: Point A(6, 1) is dilated by a scale factor of 2 with center at the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Multiply both coordinates by 2: (2 × 6, 2 × 1) = (12, 2).

items.q: Point A(4, −8) is dilated by a scale factor of 2 with center at the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Multiply both coordinates by 2: (2 × 4, 2 × −8) = (8, −16).

items.q: Point A(6, 4) is dilated by a scale factor of 2 with center at the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Multiply both coordinates by 2: (2 × 6, 2 × 4) = (12, 8).

items.q: A figure is dilated by a scale factor of 3. Is the image an enlargement or a reduction?
items.e: A scale factor greater than 1 makes the image larger. An enlargement.

items.q: Point A(6, −5) is dilated by a scale factor of 2 with center at the origin. What are the coordinates of A′?
items.e: Multiply both coordinates by 2: (2 × 6, 2 × −5) = (12, −10).

items.q: A figure is dilated by a scale factor of 2. Is the image an enlargement or a reduction?
items.e: A scale factor greater than 1 makes the image larger. An enlargement.

items.q: A dilation centered at the origin maps A(−6, 1) to A′(−12, 2). What is the scale factor?
items.e: Divide an image coordinate by the original: −12 ÷ (−6) = 2.
